A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaST0 research. All 16 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison. Visual inspection resolved extraction artifacts, and relocated material was matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLBench experiments, component ablations, six real-world Franka tasks, and a repeated-execution long-horizon evaluation in Tables I–II and Figure 4.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulation and Franka results and reports additional mobile and dexterous manipulation experiments, extended ablations, and failure cases.

M1.justification: v1 Section III-E trains the reasoning expert first, then freezes it while training the action expert; v3 Section 3.5 instead jointly optimizes both experts. Appendix B also introduces 20-dimensional mobile and 26-dimensional dexterous action interfaces with input/output MLP adaptation. The underlying multimodal latent CoT and shared-attention architecture remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds two AgileX mobile tasks, arranging dishes and sorting spoons, and two TienKung dexterous-hand tasks, opening a drawer and placing a button. These introduce coordinated base–arm control and articulated-hand manipulation. The ten RLBench tasks, six Franka tasks, long-horizon test, and Appendix A pretraining dataset mixture are retained.

E2.justification: The six RLBench comparators and three Franka comparators remain unchanged. New mobile and dexterous comparisons reuse π0.5 and CoT-VLA. SpatialVLA is omitted only from these added tasks, with poor depth estimation given as the reason; it is not removed from any matched earlier comparison.

E3.justification: The reported SFT schedule changes from 40 reasoning epochs followed by 300 action epochs to 300 joint epochs, and the backbone size description changes from 1B to 1.5B. Real-world evaluation now specifies three repetitions of 15 rollouts at different tabletop positions. New platforms introduce three-view mobile and single-view dexterous protocols. These document revised settings without establishing that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 5 extends the existing temporal-horizon sweep with five- and six-step conditions. Appendix E adds three qualitative failure cases involving incomplete wiping, plate collisions, and missed drawer grasps. The other component ablations and long-horizon analysis are retained; the full attention heatmap comparison is relocated to Appendix D rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports three repetitions of real-world evaluations and aggregate uncertainty values: LaST0 72% ±3, SpatialVLA 41% ±2, π0.5 59% ±4, and CoT-VLA 50% ±2. The statistic represented by these real-world ± values is not explicitly defined. Simulation retains three seeded evaluations and variance reporting. Newly disclosed repetition counts do not establish an actual increase in runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds four task columns, with LaST0 success rates of 0.67, 0.27, 0.87, and 0.60. Retained tables revise LaST0 Water Plants from 0.65 to 0.60, CoT-VLA egg placement from 0.53 to 0.33 and its mean from 0.53 to 0.50, and SpatialVLA's Franka mean from 0.39 to 0.41. Figure 5 adds five-/six-step results of 80%/79%. Changed training and evaluation descriptions prevent interpreting revised entries as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds mathematical definitions of the 20-dimensional mobile and 26-dimensional dexterous action vectors. The original policy factorization, interleaved latent sequence, and cosine loss remain unchanged; the factorization moves to Appendix F.1. No new theorem, proof, or theoretical guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The three central contributions—multimodal latent reasoning, temporal latent prediction, and fast–slow coordination—remain. The abstract and introduction broaden the empirical claims from six Franka tasks to ten real-world tasks across tabletop, mobile, and dexterous settings, claiming respective improvements of 13, 14, and 14 percentage points. The simulation advantage remains claimed in the introduction.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the added experiments as evidence of applicability to larger action spaces and more complex embodiments. Appendix E newly attributes failures to height/position errors, collisions, and missing visual feedback. The horizon discussion now explains choosing four steps because further extension provides no improvement, replacing the earlier emphasis on reasoning latency tradeoffs.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds platform, camera, control-vector, and MLP adaptation specifications for AgileX and TienKung. v3 also discloses the 3.3B total model size, fixed modality-ablation settings, and separate expert inference speeds. Its architecture description now agrees with the 384×384 experimental inputs already stated in v1. The explicit Tashan tactile-sensor description disappears, without establishing hardware removal, and the project-page address changes without establishing a new code release.

R1.justification: v3 removes the reinforcement-learning post-training discussion and associated citations, including GRAPE, ConRFT, and SimpleVLA-RL, alongside some background references. It adds Latent Implicit Visual Reasoning and references for the two new robot platforms. The central positioning relative to explicit CoT, LCDrive, and ThinkAct remains.

P1.justification: v3 extensively condenses and edits the abstract, related work, methods, results discussion, and conclusion. CoT preliminaries, KV-cache explanation, and detailed execution discussion move into appendices, while hardware and task descriptions are reorganized by embodiment. It also replaces numbered citations with author–year citations, updates authorship, removes the future-work paragraph, and adds an Impact Statement.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document template and appendix layout, redraws Figure 1 with embodiment examples, and removes Figure 2's training-stage panel. Table 2 gains grouped embodiment columns; the temporal-ablation plot gains bars. Setup figures are merged and relocated, execution montages are expanded, and new hardware and failure figures appear. The original complete attention grid is retained in the appendix.

improvement.justification: v1's embodiment evidence is confined to Franka configurations. v3 substantially strengthens applicability evidence through coordinated mobile manipulation and dexterous-hand experiments, accompanied by concrete control specifications and baseline comparisons. Newly reported real-world uncertainty, extended horizon analysis, and explicit failure cases improve transparency and expose practical limitations absent from v1. These gains are substantial, although each new platform has only two tasks and the revised joint-training recipe is not directly compared with staged training.
